sections.h2: What are my options for selling a house in Miami?
sections.html:
A Miami owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house in its current condition. Each route trades price against time and effort, and the right one depends on the house, the loan balance and how soon the money is needed.

Miami covers 36.00 square miles of land and held 489,812 people in the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, up 10.8 percent from the 2020 base. The 2020 density was 12,285.8 people per square mile, and housing types vary block to block, so a neighbor's sale is a weak guide to your own price.

  • List with an agent: widest exposure, but showings, repairs and a longer timeline.
  • For sale by owner: you handle pricing, paperwork and negotiation yourself.
  • Cash offer: fewer showings and a faster close, usually at a discount to a repaired, listed house.
  • Keep and rent: only if the zoning and city rules below allow the kind of rental you have in mind.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Miami homes and owners?
sections.html:
Miami is a renter-heavy city. QuickFacts shows an owner-occupied rate of 30.8 percent for 2020 to 2024, with 194,821 households averaging 2.32 people.

The median value is a citywide midpoint. A waterfront condo and an inland single-family house will land far from it, so get a written offer or an appraisal for your own address.

sections.h2: Can I rent out a Miami house short term instead of selling?
sections.html:
Usually not a single-family house or duplex. The City of Miami says houses and duplexes in T3 and T4-R transect zones are generally ineligible for short-term rental or lodging use, citing the ruling in City of Miami v. Airbnb.

Apartment and condo conversions follow a longer path. The city lists a Certificate of Occupancy, a state DBPR lodging license, a Certificate of Use, a Business Tax Receipt and any county approvals before operations may start, and the Certificate of Use renews every year.

If a rental plan falls through, owners who inherited a house or moved away often decide to sell instead. Check your zoning with the city's zoning department before you count on rental income in a sale-versus-keep comparison.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees come with a Miami sale?
sections.html:
Florida's deed stamp tax is the main transfer cost, and Miami-Dade County uses its own rate. The Department of Revenue prints 60 cents per $100 for Miami-Dade, plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax that is not due on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling. Every other county charges 70 cents per $100.

The department adds that all parties to the document are liable for the tax whoever agrees to pay it, and the tax is collected by the clerk at recording.

  • Clerk recording charges are set in section 28.24 of the Florida Statutes: $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus trust fund and technology charges.
  • Mortgage payoff, unpaid property tax and any city or county liens come out of the proceeds.
  • Ask the title company for a settlement statement before you sign.

sections.h2: How do Miami-Dade property taxes work when I sell?
sections.html:
Miami-Dade's property appraiser values property, and the county tax collector bills it. The appraiser's own site says it does not send tax bills and does not set or collect taxes.

Its notice for the 2026 roll says the property appraiser certified the tax roll on October 16, 2026, and that the countywide taxable value estimate released June 1 was $540.7 billion, a 5.5 percent increase from 2025. Appeals of a value go to the value adjustment board, and the state sets a 25-day window from the proposed tax notice for filing a petition with the clerk.

Homestead owners should know that a sale is a change of ownership. Under the state's Save Our Homes rules the next owner's assessment resets to just value the following January 1, so the seller's capped value does not pass to the buyer. A seller buying another Florida home can ask about portability, which must be filed with the homestead application by March 1.

sections.h2: What if the house has liens, repairs or code problems?
sections.html:
A cash sale can still close, but each problem has to be dealt with at or before closing. A title search shows mortgages, judgments and unpaid taxes, and unpaid property tax becomes delinquent on April 1 with tax certificates sold by June 1.

Open permits and unpermitted work are another common catch in older Miami buildings. Ask the city building department what is open on your parcel, and ask the buyer whether the offer assumes the work stays as is.

  • Inherited house: the estate may need probate before anyone can sign a deed.
  • Behind on the mortgage: ask the lender for a payoff figure and the foreclosure status in writing.
  • Tenant in place: Florida requires 3 days' written notice for unpaid rent, excluding weekends and court holidays, and a month-to-month tenancy ends with at least 30 days' notice.

sections.h2: What happens at the Miami closing table?
sections.html:
The seller signs a deed, the title company pays off liens, and the clerk of the circuit court records the deed and collects the stamp tax. The state's list of taxable deeds includes warranty, special warranty, quit claim and trustee's deeds, so the form of deed does not avoid the tax.

Miami-Dade's property appraiser site points owners to a free alert system run by the county clerk, which notifies you within 24 hours if a deed or mortgage is recorded in your name. Sign up before and after a sale so you see exactly what was filed.

After closing, tell the appraiser's office if you had a homestead exemption, and keep the settlement statement for your tax records. A homestead exemption is lost when the owner is no longer a permanent resident of the home, and the office will update the parcel after the deed records.

sections.h2: How do I check a Miami cash offer?
sections.html:
Compare it against what you would net from a listing after commission, repairs and carrying costs, and read every line of the contract. Confirm who pays the deed stamp tax, the title policy and recording charges, and what happens to the deposit.

Ask for the closing date in writing, and ask whether a title company or attorney handles the closing. Never sign a deed before the contract is final, and never pay an upfront fee to receive an offer.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell a house in Miami?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close in a couple of weeks when title is clear, while a listed sale usually takes longer because of showings, buyer financing and inspections. Liens, probate or a tenant can slow either route.

faqs.q: Does Miami-Dade charge a different deed tax than other Florida counties?
faqs.a: Yes. The Department of Revenue prints 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax for Miami-Dade, with the surtax not due when only a single-family dwelling is transferred. Other counties charge 70 cents per $100.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Miami house I inherited?
faqs.a: Yes, once someone has legal authority to sign. Florida allows summary administration when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less or the death was more than two years ago, so ask a probate attorney which path fits.

faqs.q: Will my homestead tax cap pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. A sale is a change of ownership, and the property returns to just value on the following January 1. You may be able to port your own cap to a new Florida homestead if you file by March 1.

faqs.q: Can I turn my Miami house into a short-term rental first?
faqs.a: In most cases no. The city says single-family and duplex structures in T3 and T4-R zones are generally ineligible. Confirm your zoning with the Miami zoning department before planning around rental income.
